text:
sam-support: Heads-up — ACME (acct: acme-co) opened an escalation: p99 latencies for Dedicated hotpool requests spiking to ~6-8s since 2026-03-15 12:04Z. They see consistent p95 ~120ms but p99 divergence during billing-window traffic. They attached traces showing attach wait + cold GPU start. @lee-sre @kai-platform please triage.

lee-sre: thanks. can you paste the pool id + any repro steps the customer used? also any errors (auth/500s) or just slow responses?

sam-support: pool_id=ded-hot-42. Customer repro: repeated small chat requests hitting their reserved capacity (~80% util) then a sudden burst ~3x baseline. Repro curl they provided:

```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-huge-v2","prompt":"short prompt","max_tokens":32}' \
  https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
```

Logs they pasted:
```
[12:04:23] attach_request pool=ded-hot-42 req_id=abc123 status=queued
[12:04:30] attach_attempt pool=ded-hot-42 req_id=abc123 result=attach_timeout elapsed=12.1s
[12:04:31] fallback route=reserve-fallback model=rw-medium-v2 latency=180ms
[12:04:31] request_complete req_id=abc123 total_time=7.8s
```

They also saw image-pull delays on some nodes and a few auth 401s (~0.1%) that don't correlate to most spikes.

kai-platform: initial thoughts — looks like hotpool saturation + thundering attach attempts causing cold GPU starts and some image pull noise. attach_timeout at default 12s -> requests fall back and incur extra routing time. Are they on min_pool=0 or low min_pool?

sam-support: customer config shows min_pool=1, burst_capacity=3. During peak the pool was at 100% and attach_rate spiked.

lee-sre: OK. priority triage actions: 1) Confirm if dedicated hosts were prewarmed (image cached) at time of spikes. 2) Check attach queue length and attach success/fail counts for ded-hot-42. 3) Correlate with autoscaler logs for scale-up decisions. I'll pull metrics now.

ops-bot: autoscaler_event pool=ded-hot-42 time=2026-03-15T12:03:58 event=scale_up started target_replicas=12 current_replicas=8 reason=cpu+req_rate

lee-sre: autoscaler started scale-up at 12:03:58 but nodes didn't reach ready until ~12:07 -> warmup delay ~3m. Meanwhile many attach attempts queued -> attach_timeout. Possible causes: image pull latency, node boot jitter, or kube prewarm throttle.

sam-support: customer asked for quick mitigations — they want to reduce p99 now. Suggestions?

kai-platform: immediate mitigations (quick):
- increase min_pool to 3 for this pool to reduce cold attach exposure
- enable proactive image prepull on warm nodes (prewarm images)
- bump attach_timeout to 20s to allow late attaches to succeed instead of fallback (temporary)
- enable fallback routes to smaller models only for non-critical traffic

lee-sre: operational steps I'll run now:
1) query attach queue: `k get pods -l pool=ded-hot-42 -o json | jq` to see pull status
2) check registry response times and node image-pull logs (timestamp 12:03-12:10)
3) inspect kubelet backoff events on new nodes
4) correlate with provisioning logs: cloud API rate limits?

anita-cust: thanks — their app is user-facing so increasing min_pool is ok for short window. they asked whether warmup prepull can be automated.

kai-platform: yes we have a gating flag to enable proactive prepull per pool. I'll flip it on for ded-hot-42 and increase min_pool to 3 (temporary). Also will schedule an image-cache sweep during low-traffic window.

lee-sre: found one pattern: 2 of the new nodes during scaleup logged repeated image-pull 429 from registry (rate limit) causing kubelet retries and long InitContainers. that explains most of the 3m warmup. recommending: temporarily widen registry rate limit for infra, and add image pull retries with exponential backoff tuned.

sam-support: I've notified ACME of proposed mitigations (min_pool bump + prepull + attach_timeout bump). they approved immediate min_pool change.

ops-bot: config_change user=kai-platform pool=ded-hot-42 min_pool:1->3 prewarm_images=true attach_timeout:12->20

lee-sre: after change, monitor p99 over next 30m. also create a follow-up ticket for infra to request registry quota increase and to add image caching nodes in the region.

kai-platform: created infra ticket INFRA-4821 for registry quota and image cache nodes. also adding automated prewarm policy to the pool template.

sam-support: ACME reports improvement: p99 dropped to ~350ms within 8 minutes of changes. they still saw a single 1.2s spike when a rare auth 401 happened; we think that's unrelated.

lee-sre: great. next steps (postmortem):
- primary cause: hotpool saturation + registry rate limit causing node warmup delays -> attach timeouts -> fallback and higher p99
- short-term: increased min_pool, enabled prepull, bumped attach_timeout
- medium-term: registry quota increase, dedicated image cache + prewarming during predicted windows, autoscaler tuning to avoid large batch scaleups (stagger start)
- long-term: add faster fallback path that uses warm standby models in same pool to avoid cross-pool routing latency

anita-cust: appreciate the fast response. pls keep us posted when infra ticket closes.

sam-support: will follow up. closing thread once INFRA-4821 has updates. :thumbsup:
